title: Purdue feature traces the community roots of ELARA's robotics research
summary: A Purdue Polytechnic profile connects Chorong Park's technology-support work with older adults to ELARA's approach to AI and companion robots.

sources.label: Purdue Polytechnic: a healthier future for aging through embodied AI

paragraphs.text: Purdue Polytechnic has featured Chorong Park's path from graduate research at Purdue to community-engaged work at ELARA Lab, University of Houston. Written by Nick Pompella and published October 21, the profile explores how older adults help shape research on AI and companion robots.

Sharing the feature on October 26, Park reflected on more than 500 hours spent helping older adults with technology during her Ph.D. Purdue's account identifies the Tippecanoe Senior Center as a setting for that work, which current Purdue students continue.

For Park, those conversations exposed the gap between what seems straightforward to a designer and what someone actually experiences. She credits them with shaping a research approach in which older adults help decide what support belongs in their lives, rather than simply testing a finished design.

The feature also describes her continuing collaborations with Purdue faculty, connecting work on accessibility, human-robot interaction, immersive technology and aging with ELARA's research in Houston.
